A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Video Interface Networks study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite additions and renumbering in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original VBench evaluations, optical-flow analyses, architectural ablations, qualitative results, and a human preference study, including supplementary comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds an operation-level computational-cost analysis in Section 7 and Figure 13.

M1.justification: The VIN architecture, global-token conditioning, joint denoising objective, local context, stop-gradient operation, and inference-time token fusion are unchanged. Equations 1–10 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same reported 840,000-video training corpus, VBench prompt suite, video-length coverage, and user-study prompts. The added FLOPs breakdown introduces no new dataset, task, or test scenario.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Full Attention, AutoReg., StreamingT2V, FreeNoise, Spectral Blending, and the supplementary OpenSora v1.2, Mochi-1, and HunyuanVideo models. The new FLOPs breakdown continues the existing VIN-versus-Full-Attention comparison.

E3.justification: Resolution, model configuration, chunk sizes, sampling steps, evaluation metrics, video lengths, and user-study procedures remain unchanged. Section 7 disaggregates the existing FLOPs analysis without reporting changed evaluation conditions.

E4.justification: v2 adds a supplementary efficiency analysis separating QKV projection, attention, feedforward, and VIN-module costs across video lengths (Section 7, Figure 13). Existing architectural ablations, chunk-transition analyses, and attention visualizations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three generated videos per evaluation prompt and two samples per ablation prompt, with the same shared-noise control for the global-token comparison. No new run-count disclosures, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Figure 13 adds component-level relative FLOPs results at 128, 256, and 512 frames. Existing benchmark, ablation, human-study, and qualitative results are unchanged; Tables 1 and 2 retain identical numerical entries.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and derivations remain unchanged. New Table 3 summarizes existing notation, while Section 7 elaborates the existing quadratic-attention motivation without adding a theorem, proof, or substantive formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about parallel video generation, temporal consistency, motion quality, computational savings, and human preference. The new efficiency breakdown supports an existing contribution.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly interprets the cost breakdown: QKV and feedforward costs are similar, VIN processing adds modest overhead, and savings arise chiefly from reduced attention costs. Existing interpretations and limitations concerning generation-only learning remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 explicitly instructs readers to view videos through index.html in the supplementary folder; v2 removes that instruction. The abstract's video link, implementation settings, and training/inference algorithms remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Seitzer et al., Bridging the Gap to Real-World Object-Centric Learning, as bibliography entry [10]. The related-work discussion and positioning otherwise remain unchanged; subsequent reference-number shifts do not represent additional works.

P1.justification: v2 adds short glossary and FLOPs-breakdown sections and an acknowledgment, removes the separate supplementary title and preamble, and updates cross-references. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds notation Table 3 and stacked FLOPs Figure 13. Early appendix material is reflowed, including relocation of the existing supplementary VBench plot and qualitative examples; existing scientific displays are retained.

improvement.justification: Section 7 and Figure 13 make the source of computational savings more assessable than v1's aggregate efficiency reporting, while Table 3 provides a convenient notation reference. These are useful, limited gains with the principal scientific evidence unchanged. Removing the supplementary-folder viewing instruction slightly reduces access guidance, although the existing video link remains.
